materialInputDiagnostic.scope: Own experimental raw Rust physics2d kernel World; separate from the current Rapier-backed TypeScript facade.
materialInputDiagnostic.interpretation: The diagnostic asserts reproduction of the existing defect; it is not a production acceptance test blessing nonfinite state. No production fix or API policy has been chosen.

contract.currentShapeDefDocumentation: world.rs:132-134 documents density only as kilograms per square metre; default is 1.0.
contract.currentCreateShapeDocumentation: world.rs:403-404 says adds the core and recomputes mass; returns u32, with no material Result/error or documented panic.
contract.bounds: No finite >0 material contract, minimum density, maximum density, representable derived-mass/inverse-mass bound, or material error behavior is defined for this raw Rust entry in ShapeDef/create_shape docs, physics2d README kernel-development section, or LIM-527.
contract.whatFixMustDefine: An explicit accepted input/derived-mass range and error behavior, or arithmetic that preserves finite mass state over the intended range, before committing a regression expectation. Even a finite positive-only check would not cover f32::from_bits(1).

owningCause: World::create_shape appends the material and shape then calls update_mass without validating material values or derived mass properties (world.rs:404-409).
Infinity: mass_of returns infinite mass; update_mass accumulates first += center * infinite mass, so the centered unit box produces 0*infinity NaNs (world.rs:453-460).
Smallest positive f32: unit-box mass rounds to f32::from_bits(1); 1/mass overflows to infinity inside first.scale(1/mass), turning zero first moments into NaN local_center (world.rs:460).
Both: NaN local_center then contaminates parallel-axis inertia and the world center before any solver visit; update_mass also publishes an infinite inverse mass for the tiny case (world.rs:461-487).
materialInputDiagnostic.observedSummary: Both bad values are accepted without panic and produce NaN center immediately. One subsequent ordinary World::step does not panic, leaves the center NaN, misses the ground contact, and retains finite velocity [0,-0.16350001]. Nonfinite velocity was NOT observed or claimed in this minimal fixture. Ordinary density 1 stays finite and forms one contact/constraint.
